<reflection>
The low-catalyst + product experiment has further separated several mechanisms. M4, M5, M14, M16, M17, M20 are now clearly worse fits. The top group (M6, M8, M2, M18, M1, M10, M15, M13, M19) is still tightly bunched. 

M6 and M8 (catalyst activation) are now slight leaders. But M1 is close too, suggesting the baseline Michaelis-Menten is still quite good.

To discriminate M6/M8 (activation mechanisms, showing induction) from M1 and other deactivation mechanisms, I need an experiment where:
- Induction period would be clearly visible: low catalyst concentration to stretch time scale, but with concentrated substrate to make product formation clearly detectable
- OR: stepwise sequential runs would help, but we only vary initial conditions

The key is that M6 (cat=>cat*) and M8 (cat<=>cat* + L) predict a slow approach to steady-state rate (induction), while M1 predicts immediate maximum rate followed by substrate depletion. M2, M13 (dimerization) predict rate dips with high [cat].

A high substrate, very low catalyst run would give a long time window, but we already did similar conditions. 

Let me instead probe with HIGH catalyst to amplify bimolecular mechanisms (M2, M13, M18, M19, M3) differences from unimolecular (M1, M6, M8, M9, M14):
- At high [cat], M2/M13 strongly suppress effective catalyst
- M18 (2catS→) strongly enhanced
- M19 (cat+catS) strongly enhanced
- M6/M8 activation would be saturated
- M1 scales linearly

High catalyst + high substrate pushes turnover heavy on all pathways.
</reflection>

I'll run a very high catalyst loading experiment (near upper limit) with moderate substrate and no product. This will:
- Strongly test bimolecular cat deactivation/dimerization (M2, M3, M13, M18, M19)

- Make substrate inhibition mechanisms (M7, M11, M16) differ from others since they're first-order in S
- No product initially — so deactivation kinetics can be cleanly separated from product inhibition
</hypothesis>
